basis: Inherited dystroglycan glycosylation disorder causing skeletal myopathy; brain and eye abnormalities are confined mainly to severe subtypes.
Benign smooth-muscle tumour arising in the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no axis.
Inherited PRNP-mediated neurodegeneration causing chorea and dementia; genetic prion misfolding does not establish an infectious or immune mechanism.
Inherited ventricular electrical disorder causing ventricular fibrillation.
Open spinal neural-tube and vertebral defect; neurogenic bladder with impaired urinary function occurs in roughly 80-90%.
Toxic injury and degeneration of the retinal macula.
Extrauterine smooth-muscle tumour nodules predominantly occupy the lungs; uterine origin is outside the axes. Heart and spinal involvement are rare.
Inherited red-cell methemoglobin disorder; destructive neurologic disease is mainly an uncommon generalized reductase-deficiency subtype, under ~30% overall.
Defined by camptodactyly, joint contractures and facial skeletal dysplasia; associated clubfoot and dysostosis are skeletal.
Defined by B-cell deficiency, distal skeletal anomalies and urogenital malformations including urethral/urinary defects; recurrent infections are separate diseases.
Predominantly uterine/placental trophoblastic cancer; ovarian and testicular origins also lack an axis. Lung metastases are not established at >=30% across all cases.
GPI-anchor glycosylation disorder with CNS and skeletal disease; visual dysfunction 4/4. Urinary defects (3/4), hearing and cardiac defects (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Defined by developmental impairment, sometimes epilepsy; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage, and visual impairment is less frequent.
Benign neoplasm arising in or occupying the heart.
Inherited sensory peripheral neuropathy causing sensory ataxia; definition excludes ulcerating acropathy and autonomic abnormalities.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across chromosome 1p deletions; other organ abnormalities depend on the deleted interval.
Defined by microcephaly, abnormal cortical development and cerebellar hypoplasia; eye and skeletal findings in isolated assessed patients do not establish >=30%.
Tumours arise from or directly involve central or peripheral autonomic nervous tissue; endocrine activity is not universal across the group.
Skeletal dysplasia, high myopia and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; upper-airway obstruction 80-99%. Cleft palate (80-99%; gastrointestinal) omitted by cap.
Secondary glaucoma caused by ocular trauma damages the eye and optic nerve.
Inherited transport/metabolic disorder with cataracts and renal tubulopathy; intellectual disability and neurologic dysfunction 80-99%. Skeletal disease (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Benign epithelial tumour arising in sphenoid sinus respiratory mucosa; paranasal sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
Broad substance-related umbrella without a shared damaged organ; hepatic, pancreatic, cardiac and fetal neurologic disease belong to distinct subtypes.
Hyperplastic proliferation of the urinary tract urothelium.
Anterior segment dysgenesis with Peters anomaly and cataract; both defining abnormalities affect the eye.
